rows.09:08ac:
Nice to meet you all.
I'm Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
Well then, I'll tell the second story.
Um... what do you all think of the old school building?
I imagine you find it frightening?{p}{f:What|What} about you, {a}?
rows.09:0b20:
Rounds are necessary, after all.
There's no telling when a thief might break in during the night, and outsiders might start sleeping there without permission.
Though there's nothing in there worth stealing.
So why did even the rounds come to an end?
...There's a reason for that.
That's the story I'll tell you.{p}
rows.09:0fb8:
That was Mr. Sakurai.
It's not that Mr. Sakurai wasn't scared.
If anything, he may have been more easily frightened than most.
Even so, he also had a stronger sense of responsibility than most.
He just couldn't cut corners the way the other teachers did.
There were even people who laughed behind Mr. Sakurai's back for patrolling the old school building so seriously.
Night duty didn't come around very often, but whenever his turn drew near, Mr. Sakurai's heart grew heavy all the same.
And then, once again, his turn for night duty came around.{p}
rows.09:18fc:
When he had more or less finished checking the three-story old school building, he hurried back to the night-duty room.
Shut up tight as it had been, the night-duty room was like a steam bath.
"...Ugh. I should've left a window open."
Grading the tests he had given that day, Mr. Sakurai thought idly about the old school building.
What had he been so afraid of?
It had been the same as always; nothing at all was different.
No one would ever sneak into an old school building like that.
He was only making the rounds to be ready for that one-in-a-million chance, that was all.
When he finished grading and casually glanced out the window... he saw a faint light mixed in with the darkness.
rows.09:2a38:
"...Tch. You're a stubborn one."
Clicking his tongue, Mr. Sakurai had no choice but to make the first move himself.
rows.09:3ba4:
Mr. Sakurai stomped all over the floor, deliberately making his footsteps loud, and walked around with no aim at all.
And would you believe it, the footsteps followed right along with him.
Whenever Mr. Sakurai walked, he heard the footsteps.
What's more, the other footsteps matched his own exactly, every bit as loud.
Always from behind him...
And whenever he stopped walking, the footsteps stopped dead too, as if they were reading Mr. Sakurai's mind.{p}
rows.09:3fbc: And the distance, which had stayed more or less the same, began closing, closer and closer.
rows.09:4f2c: Relying on the feeble light of her flashlight, she climbed the stairs, creak, creak, testing each step so she wouldn't miss her footing.{p}
rows.09:6478:
Relying on the feeble light of his flashlight, he climbed the stairs, creak, creak, testing each step so he wouldn't miss his footing.
When he reached the top, Mr. Sakurai couldn't believe his eyes.{p}
rows.09:5330:
There was a ripping sound, something tearing.
"Huh..."
She had gotten caught on a protruding nail and had been struggling against it.
"How awful!
This blouse cost a fortune!
Argh, I'm so mad!"
It was her own fault for jumping to conclusions, but she conveniently ignored that and sulked, I'm told.{p}
rows.09:5998:
"Ahahaha, ah-ah-ah, ah-hah!"
The baby laughed on her right shoulder.
"Eeek☆"
People are strange in moments like this. You know you should leave well enough alone, yet you end up doing the exact opposite of what you should.
rows.09:5b90:
The next morning, she was found at the entrance of the old school building, laughing like a baby,
"Ahahaha, ah-ah-ah, ah-hah!"
and sucking on her fingers.
I heard this later: some time before, a newborn baby had been abandoned in the old school building.
Yes, by the time it was found, the baby was no longer breathing.
Apparently, if it had been found sooner, it might have been saved.
The teacher who had neglected the patrol back then came in for a lot of criticism.{p}
rows.09:71f4:
He switched on the flashlight in his hand and lit up his feet.
"This is bad, look at all this blood..."
Then, the moment he tried to yank his foot out of the hole with all his might, it popped out with surprising ease.
Carried by his own force, he tumbled backward and crashed into a pillar.
"Ow, ow... When it rains, it pours."
And just as he was about to get up, the grinning man from before was peering down at him from directly above.{p}
rows.09:78d0:
"Oh, here goes nothing!"
Mr. Sakurai spun around and leapt straight at it.
"Ugh☆"
There was definitely someone standing there.
Mr. Sakurai had the figure locked tight in his arms.
He had never expected the intruder to be exactly where he'd guessed, so he was startled, and at the same time froze where he was.
The thing was scrawnier than he'd expected, and seemed to be wearing something damp, stiff and musty-smelling.
"This could be the end!
I'm done for!
...?"
Eerily, the thing did nothing...
Both the teacher and the thing held that position, motionless, for a while.{p}
rows.09:8440:
"Oh no!"
The jolt of the fall seemed to have switched the flashlight on.
"Well, if it's come to this..."
Mr. Sakurai hurriedly snatched it up,{p}
